final_candidates.decision_summary: Removes a positive charge in the H1 Sb antigenic site, plausibly disrupting antibody contacts while likely tolerated.
Alters a surface-exposed charged residue near antigenically important loops, with moderate escape potential and folding risk.
Introduces a potential N-glycosylation site in a known antigenic region, likely shielding epitopes with generally acceptable fitness.

stop_reason.detail: Further self-iteration is unlikely to improve ranking without external functional or antigenic screening.

history.rationale: Creates an N-X-S glycosylation sequon (N157-S158-S159) in a surface antigenic loop, likely shielding antibody epitopes while removing a positive charge.
Retained as the strongest current candidate; removes a positive charge in the H1 Sb antigenic site and is a plausible escape substitution while likely retaining fitness.
Adds an N-X-S sequon (N137-S138-S139) on a solvent-exposed region, predicted to add N-linked glycan masking without disrupting core folding.
Retained because E137N alters a surface-exposed charged side chain near antigenically important loops, likely contributing to escape with moderate folding risk.
Introduces a glycan sequon (N156-K157-S158) and alters the antigenic loop adjacent to K157, likely reducing antibody recognition.
Retained as a glycosylation-creating substitution in a known H1 antigenic region, potentially shielding epitopes while being generally tolerated.
Replaces a small polar surface residue with a bulky hydrophobic aromatic side chain, likely disrupting antibody contacts in an antigenic site while preserving local folding.
Retained because a hydrophobic substitution at this antigenic site position can disrupt antibody contacts, though fitness cost is somewhat more uncertain.
Introduces a charged glutamate in a surface loop, likely altering epitope electrostatics and antibody recognition while retaining backbone flexibility.
Retained as a charge-introducing change in the Sb site, likely immunogenically disruptive, with some concern about structural penalty.
Removes a solvent-exposed positive charge and changes side-chain shape, predicted to reduce antibody binding without disrupting global folding.
Retained as a charge-removing substitution in the same antigenic region; plausible escape, with lower confidence due to less certain effect magnitude.
Charge reversal at a surface-exposed residue in an antigenic loop likely disrupts complementary antibody interactions while maintaining local stability.
Retained because reversing charge at K187 may strongly alter antibody recognition, although it may reduce receptor-binding or stability.
Added as a less hydrophobic alternative to S159F at the same antigenic position, potentially preserving fitness better while still altering the epitope.
Added as a charge-inserting substitution in the H1 Sb antigenic site; may promote escape, but fitness cost is uncertain and therefore confidence is moderate.
Added as a conservative hydrophobic substitution adjacent to antigenic residues; lower predicted escape magnitude but likely better tolerated.
